rcolapi

rcolapi is an R client for the Catalogue of Life via the ChecklistBank API (https://api.checklistbank.org). It allows you to verify and match scientific names, retrieve hierarchical classifications, look up datasets, taxa, synonyms, vernacular names, and geographic distributions, and run ChecklistBank parsers — against any public dataset in ChecklistBank or the latest Catalogue of Life release. It is modelled on the conventions of rgbif and taxadb.

Note on Origin & Architectural Evolution: This package builds upon the original rcol project by Catalogue of Life (https://catalogueoflife.github.io/rcol/). This version introduces substantial architectural enhancements to simplify scientific workflows, including:

  • Direct Scientific Name Support: Pass scientific names directly (e.g., "Panthera leo" or "Werneria nubigena") to downstream functions without needing prior manual ID lookups.
  • Vectorized Multi-Species Queries: Seamlessly pass character vectors of multiple species (e.g., c("Werneria nubigena", "Panthera leo")) and receive clean, concatenated tidy data frames.
  • Distribution Traceability: Multi-species distributions include input_row and scientific_name, preserving their association with the original input.
  • Clean Name Verification: col_check_name() returns an essential 9-column resolution summary showing accepted names, status, and IDs.
  • Flexible Classification Extraction: col_classification() supports both Long format and Wide format (wide = TRUE).

There are two parallel families of functions:

  • col_*() convenience functions that target the latest extended Catalogue of Life release ("3LXR"). On first use, the release key is pinned in session (col_key()), ensuring long-running jobs are never disrupted by mid-session release updates. Use col_refresh() to re-pin.
  • clb_*() universal low-level functions that accept an explicit dataset = argument (e.g., "COL25", 2099) to query any dataset in ChecklistBank.

Installation

The package is now named rcolapi; load it with library(rcolapi). The col_*() and clb_*() function names are unchanged. This package is not the archived CRAN package rcol. The GitHub repository is PaulESantos/rcolapi.

Version 0.0.2 is being prepared for CRAN submission. Until it is accepted, install this version from GitHub:

# install.packages("pak")
pak::pak("PaulESantos/rcolapi")

# or
# install.packages("remotes")
remotes::install_github("PaulESantos/rcolapi")

Documentation is published at https://paulesantos.github.io/rcolapi/.

After CRAN accepts rcolapi, the CRAN installation command will be:

install.packages("rcolapi")

Quick start

1. Name Verification & Matching 

library(rcolapi)

# High-level clean verification (9 columns) for 1 or multiple species
col_check_name(c("Werneria nubigena", "Panthera leo", "Schinus molle"))

# Detailed matching against the latest Catalogue of Life release
col_match("Panthera leo")

# Disambiguate with rank and nomenclatural code
col_match("Abies alba", rank = "species", code = "botanical")

# See all candidate matches (homonyms), not just the best one
col_match_verbose("Oenanthe")

# Match many names at once in parallel
col_match_checklist(c("Panthera leo", "Bufo bufo", "Abies alba"))

To match against a specific dataset instead of the latest COL release, use the clb_*() form with a dataset = key or alias:

clb_match("Felis catus", dataset = "COL25")          # 2025 annual release
clb_match("Macrocystis pyrifera", dataset = 2099)    # public dataset by key

2. Classification, Synonyms, Vernaculars & Distribution

The following lookup functions accept scientific names, IDs, vectors, or match result tables:

# Hierarchical classification in Wide or Long format
col_classification("Schinus molle", wide = TRUE)

# Synonyms for 1 or multiple species
col_synonyms(c("Werneria nubigena", "Panthera leo"))

# Vernacular / common names with species association (scientific_name column)
col_vernacular(c("Werneria nubigena", "Panthera leo"))

# Geographic distribution in tidy format
col_distribution(c("Werneria nubigena", "Schinus molle"))

# Details of a name usage
col_usage("Panthera leo")

3. Tree Navigation & Search 

# Walk the COL tree roots (Domains / Realms)
roots <- col_tree()

# Get direct child species under a genus
col_children("Panthera")

# Full-text search with rank and status filters
col_usage_search("Panthera", rank = "species", status = "accepted")

4. Parsers 

# Parse a scientific name into its atomic components
clb_parse_name("Abies alba Mill. var. alpina")

Catalogue of Life Releases

The Catalogue of Life is published in two cadences (monthly and annual) and two flavours (base and extended XR). Dataset-scoped clb_*() functions take a dataset = argument; helpful aliases resolve to the latest of each:

clb_col_release("monthly")                  # "3LR"   latest monthly base
clb_col_release("monthly", extended = TRUE) # "3LXR"  latest monthly extended
clb_col_release("annual")                   # e.g. "COL25"

clb_usage_search("Felidae", dataset = "COL25")

Batch results and failures

col_match_checklist() and clb_match_checklist() keep one row per input and preserve input columns with a verbatim_ prefix. Inspect match and error before interpreting the results:

match error Meaning
TRUE NA A matching usage was returned.
FALSE NA The request succeeded but no match was found.
NA Message The request or response parsing failed. 
batch <- col_match_checklist(c("Panthera leo", "Schinus molle"))
failed <- batch[is.na(batch$match), ]
unmatched <- batch[!is.na(batch$match) & !batch$match, ]
matched <- batch[!is.na(batch$match) & batch$match, ]
failed[c("verbatim_name", "error")]

These per-row diagnostics apply to batch requests. Failures before requests are submitted, such as resolving col_key(), still raise an error. The simpler col_check_name() summary retains match = NA for failed rows but does not include the error column; use col_match_checklist() when diagnosing failures.

Distribution provenance and raw responses

For multiple inputs, col_distribution() includes input_row (the one-based position in the input), scientific_name, and area. A species can have several rows after splitting semicolon-separated areas. Species with no distribution records contribute no rows, so use input_row rather than row position to join results back to your input.

species <- c("Panthera leo", "Schinus molle")
distribution <- col_distribution(species)
distribution$queried_name <- species[distribution$input_row]

# Add status, gazetteer, remarks and reference metadata
col_distribution(species, full = TRUE)

# Resolve an ID or a verification result before formatting the classification
col_classification("4CGXP", wide = TRUE)
verified <- col_check_name("Schinus molle")
col_classification(verified, wide = TRUE)

# Keep nested API responses intact and aligned with each input
responses <- col_usage(species, .raw = TRUE)
responses[[1]]

For a single input, distribution output defaults to area; full = TRUE also includes scientific_name and metadata. Usage, classification, synonym, vernacular and distribution lookups with multiple inputs and .raw = TRUE return a list of complete parsed responses, including empty responses, instead of combining them into a tibble. With one input, .raw = TRUE returns the single parsed response. For classification, .raw = TRUE takes precedence over wide.

When passing a result table to a taxon lookup, valid IDs are selected in order from accepted_id, usage_id, and id, skipping missing or empty values. Unresolved rows raise an error. Filter failed and unmatched rows before passing a batch result to a downstream lookup.

Building documentation and running tests

Online examples are displayed without execution when the README and vignettes are built. This allows documentation builds without contacting ChecklistBank. Unit tests run without API access; live integration tests are opt-in and remain skipped on CRAN.

devtools::test()

# Run live integration tests in a development session with Internet access
withr::with_envvar(c(RCOL_LIVE_TESTS = "true"), devtools::test())

# Build and check the package, including its vignettes and PDF manual
devtools::check(cran = TRUE, manual = TRUE)

Documentation builds require Pandoc; the PDF manual also requires a working LaTeX installation. These tools are separate from access to the API.

Configuration

The base URL defaults to the production API and can be redirected with the CLB_BASE_URL environment variable:

Sys.setenv(CLB_BASE_URL = "https://api.dev.checklistbank.org")
